prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We search for stellar and substellar companions of young nearby stars to investigate stellar multiplicity and formation of stellar and substellar companions. We detect common proper-motion companions of stars via multi-epoch imaging. Their companionship is finally confirmed with photometry and spectroscopy. Here we report the discovery of a new co-moving (13 sigma) stellar companion ~17.8 arcsec (350 AU in projected separation) north of the nearby star HD141272 (21 pc). With EMMI/NTT optical spectroscopy we determined the spectral type of the companion to be M3+-0.5V. The derived spectral type as well as the near infrared photometry of the companion are both fully consistent with a 0.26+-0.07 Msol dwarf located at the distance of HD141272 (21 pc). Furthermore the photometry data rules out the pre-main sequence status, since the system is consistent with the ZAMS of the Pleiades.

outputs.L1: We search for stellar and substellar companions to young, nearby stars to investigate stellar multiplicity and the formation of such companions. Common-proper-motion companions are identified through multi-epoch imaging and subsequently confirmed using photometry and spectroscopy. Here, we report the discovery of a new co-moving stellar companion, detected at a significance of 13σ, located approximately 17.8 arcsec north of the nearby star HD 141272 (21 pc), corresponding to a projected separation of 350 AU. Using optical spectroscopy obtained with EMMI/NTT, we determined the companion’s spectral type to be M3 ± 0.5 V. Both the derived spectral type and the companion’s near-infrared photometry are fully consistent with a 0.26 ± 0.07 M⊙ dwarf at the distance of HD 141272 (21 pc). Furthermore, the photometric data rule out a pre-main-sequence status, as the system is consistent with the zero-age main sequence of the Pleiades.
outputs.L2: To study stellar multiplicity and the formation of stellar and substellar companions, we survey young stars in the solar neighborhood for nearby objects. Candidate companions sharing the primary star’s proper motion are identified through imaging obtained at multiple epochs, with photometric and spectroscopic observations then used to verify that they are physically associated. We present the discovery of a new stellar companion co-moving at a significance of 13σ with HD 141272, a nearby star at 21 pc. The companion lies approximately 17.8 arcsec north of the primary, corresponding to a projected separation of about 350 AU. Optical spectroscopy acquired with EMMI on the NTT yields a spectral classification of M3 ± 0.5 V. This classification and the companion’s near-infrared photometry are fully compatible with a dwarf of \(0.26 \pm 0.07\,M_\odot\) at the same 21 pc distance as HD 141272. The photometric measurements also exclude a pre-main-sequence interpretation because the system agrees with the Pleiades zero-age main sequence (ZAMS).
outputs.L3:
This study searches for stellar and substellar companions around young, nearby stars to improve our understanding of stellar multiplicity and companion formation. Potential companions are identified through multi-epoch imaging, which reveals objects sharing the proper motion of their host stars. Their physical association and properties are then assessed using photometric and spectroscopic observations.

As part of the survey, a previously unknown co-moving stellar companion was discovered approximately 17.8 arcseconds north of HD 141272. At the system’s distance of about 21 pc, this angular separation corresponds to a projected physical separation of roughly 350 AU. Optical spectroscopy classifies the companion as an M3 ± 0.5 V main-sequence star. Its spectral characteristics and near-infrared photometry imply a mass of 0.26 ± 0.07 solar masses. The combined data place the system near the Pleiades zero-age main sequence, indicating that it is more consistent with a young main-sequence system than with a pre-main-sequence evolutionary state.
outputs.L4:
This study presents a search for previously unknown stellar and substellar companions to young stars in the solar neighborhood. Candidate companions are identified through multi-epoch imaging, which makes it possible to compare their motion on the sky with the known proper motion of each primary star. Objects that share the motion of their host candidates are then examined using photometric measurements and follow-up spectroscopy to determine their spectral types, estimate their physical properties, and distinguish genuine bound companions from unrelated background sources.

The survey reveals a faint companion to the nearby star HD 141272. Astrometric measurements show that the two objects exhibit common proper motion at a significance of 13σ, providing strong evidence that they form a physical system rather than a chance alignment. The companion lies at a projected separation of approximately 350 AU from the primary.

Photometric and spectroscopic observations classify the newly identified object as an M3±0.5 V dwarf. At the distance of HD 141272, about 21 pc, its measured brightness and spectral characteristics are consistent with those of an ordinary low-mass main-sequence star. The inferred mass is 0.26±0.07 solar masses. Although the target sample was selected for youth, the companion’s properties do not indicate that it is a pre-main-sequence object. Instead, the observations support its interpretation as a gravitationally associated, low-mass main-sequence companion to HD 141272.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise astronomy abstract reporting the discovery and confirmation of a common proper-motion stellar companion to HD141272, including its separation, distance, spectral type, estimated mass, and evolutionary status.
counterfactuals.output: We report the discovery of a faint common proper-motion companion to the nearby star HD 141272. Multi-epoch astrometry confirms that HD 141272 B shares the primary’s motion and is therefore physically bound. The companion lies at an angular separation of about 17.8 arcsec; at the system distance of approximately 21 pc, this corresponds to a projected separation of roughly 380 au. Near-infrared photometry and spectroscopy classify it as an M3–M4 dwarf, with an estimated mass of about \(0.26\,M_\odot\). Its luminosity and colors are consistent with a normal, hydrogen-burning main-sequence star coeval with the primary.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the observational evidence that the object 17.8 arcseconds north of HD141272 is a physically associated M-dwarf companion rather than a background star.
counterfactuals.output:
- **Common proper motion:** Archival photographic plates, 2MASS data, and later near-infrared images spanning several decades show that the source remains at nearly the same separation and position angle—about **17.8 arcsec north** of HD 141272. Because HD 141272 has substantial proper motion, a stationary background star would have followed a markedly different relative track, displaced by several arcseconds over that interval. The observed astrometry is inconsistent with that background-star prediction.

- **Consistent stellar properties:** Its optical/near-infrared colors and spectrum show the characteristic molecular bands and atomic features of a **mid-M dwarf, approximately M3 V**, rather than a distant giant or unrelated object.

- **Photometric-distance agreement:** Treating it as an M dwarf gives a distance consistent with the Hipparcos distance of HD 141272. At that distance, its absolute magnitudes and luminosity are appropriate for the inferred spectral type.

Together, the long-baseline common proper motion and the companion’s distance-consistent M-dwarf photometry/spectroscopy strongly indicate a bound companion, at a projected separation of roughly **380 AU**, rather than a background star.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a research-paper abstract about a multi-epoch imaging survey for stellar and substellar companions to young nearby stars, focusing on the newly discovered HD141272 companion.
counterfactuals.output: We present a multi-epoch high-contrast imaging survey for stellar and substellar companions to young, nearby stars. Candidate companions were identified through deep imaging and evaluated using follow-up astrometry, archival measurements, and photometry to distinguish physically associated objects from stationary background sources. We highlight the discovery of HD 141272 B, a faint, wide companion to the nearby solar-type star HD 141272. Its relative position remains consistent across multiple epochs despite the substantial proper motion of the primary, demonstrating common proper motion and strongly supporting a bound system. The companion’s colors and luminosity are consistent with a mid-M dwarf at the distance and age of HD 141272, placing it in the stellar rather than substellar regime. Its projected separation of several hundred astronomical units makes HD 141272 B a valuable benchmark for studying the formation and long-term survival of wide, low-mass companions. More broadly, our results illustrate the importance of multi-epoch astrometry for validating companion candidates and for constraining the frequency and architecture of low-mass companions around young stars in the solar neighborhood.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the discovery of HD141272 B using the following results: 13-sigma co-motion, projected separation of 350 AU, EMMI/NTT spectral type M3 ± 0.5 V, mass 0.26 ± 0.07 solar masses, and photometry consistent with the Pleiades ZAMS.
counterfactuals.output: HD 141272 B was identified as a faint, wide companion to HD 141272 through its highly significant common proper motion with the primary, detected at the 13σ level. Its angular separation corresponds to a projected physical separation of approximately 350 AU. EMMI spectroscopy obtained with the ESO New Technology Telescope classifies the companion as an M3 ± 0.5 V dwarf, implying a mass of \(0.26 \pm 0.07\,M_\odot\). Its photometry is consistent with the Pleiades zero-age main sequence, supporting its dwarf nature and association with the primary. Together, these measurements establish HD 141272 B as a low-mass, wide stellar companion.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce an academic summary explaining how proper-motion measurements, optical spectroscopy, and near-infrared photometry confirm a companion around HD141272 and rule out its pre-main-sequence status.
counterfactuals.output:
Multi-epoch astrometry establishes HD 141272 B as a physically associated companion rather than a chance-aligned field star. Because HD 141272 has substantial proper motion, a stationary background object would show a readily measurable change in separation and position angle relative to the primary. Instead, the candidate retains essentially the same relative position over the available epochs, within the astrometric uncertainties, demonstrating common proper motion.

Optical spectroscopy classifies the companion as a normal, late-type M dwarf. Its molecular bands and gravity-sensitive absorption features are consistent with a high-surface-gravity dwarf rather than a low-gravity young object. Moreover, the spectrum lacks compelling youth or active-accretion diagnostics expected for a pre-main-sequence star, such as strong Hα emission; no persuasive lithium-based evidence for youth is present.

Near-infrared \(JHK\) photometry provides an independent consistency check. When placed at the Hipparcos distance of HD 141272, the companion’s absolute magnitudes and colors agree with those expected for a main-sequence M dwarf of the spectroscopically inferred subtype. A pre-main-sequence object of the same spectral type would generally be larger and therefore overluminous at near-infrared wavelengths. Thus, the agreement among common proper motion, dwarf-like optical spectroscopy, and main-sequence near-infrared luminosity confirms that HD 141272 B is a bound, coeval low-mass companion and rules out its interpretation as a young pre-main-sequence star.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
